findings.title: Date overrides bypass booking and calendar conflict checks
findings.body: When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before the later `busy.every(...)` check. A date override should replace normal working hours, not make an already-booked or calendar-busy period available. This can expose slots that overlap existing bookings and allow double-booking the host.

findings.title: Fixed-host working hours are not checked for full-slot containment
findings.body: This uses `find` to reject a slot if any same-day working-hours row does not contain its start, rather than checking that one row contains the whole slot. If the host has no row for that weekday, the check falls through and treats them as available; with split hours, a valid slot in a later window can be rejected because it is outside an earlier window. Also, `end` is set to the slot start, so an event that runs past the end of a window is accepted. Round-robin slots can therefore be offered when a fixed host is unavailable, or hidden when they are available.

findings.title: Date-override validation accepts partial overlaps and rejects later windows
findings.body: These comparisons only reject slots wholly before or after an override; they do not require the entire slot to fit inside the override. For example, a 09:30–10:30 slot passes a 10:00–11:00 override even though it starts before availability. The `find` also stops at the first disjoint override, so a slot in a later same-day window (such as 13:00–17:00 after a 09:00–12:00 window) can be rejected before that window is checked. Validate that the slot is fully contained in at least one applicable override.

findings.title: DST offset is calculated from the encoded instant, not the override wall time
findings.body: Override times are represented as UTC clock fields for the organizer’s local hours (for example, 14:00Z can mean 14:00 in Asia/Kolkata). Applying `.tz()` to that `Date` treats it as an actual instant, so around a DST transition it can select the offset for a different local date or time. For example, a 03:30 America/New_York override on the spring-forward date is encoded as 03:30Z, which localizes to the previous evening and uses the pre-transition offset; the generated attendee time is then shifted by an hour.

findings.title: The new regression test does not cover fixed-host round-robin overrides
findings.body: The added timezone assertion uses the existing personal-event scenario, whose fixture has no round-robin scheduling type or fixed host. Consequently, none of the new test coverage verifies the advertised fix that makes a fixed host’s date override constrain round-robin availability.

findings.title: The added slot assertion can pass when expected slots are missing
findings.body: This assertion uses `toHaveTimeSlots`, whose implementation checks each actual slot against the expected array but does not require the actual and expected arrays to have equal lengths. If only the first of the four expected slots is returned, the assertion still passes, so the new timezone test can miss regressions that drop later slots.
